newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise in Gulf, Midcontinent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise in Gulf, Midcontinent.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices firmed in the Gulf and Midcontinent but eased in the west Texas markets as below-normal temperatures moved into the central U.S., industry sources said.
Cooler temperatures in west Texas put some slight downward pressure on Permian basin prices, but emerging heating load demand in the Midwest propped up prices in the Gulf and Midcontinent markets.
Gulf Coast gas traded in the high-$1.80s to mid-$1.90s, with Transco (Station 65) quoted as high as $2.00 and Henry Hub, La., in the low-to-mid $1.90s.

Despite the marginal strength in the Gulf markets, prices on the Appalachian pipes held steady in the $2.10-2.15 range. Temperatures are expected to drop to levels five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal by week's end in the Northeast.

As forecasters called for near-freezing temperatures tonight in most of the Midwest, buyers resurfaced, causing prices to gain about five cents to the low-to-mid $1.80s. At Demarcation, traders reported closing deals in the high $1.80s.
Although West Coast demand remained strong, Permian prices eased by a couple of cents today into the high $1.70s to low $1.80s. Cooler weather in Texas resulted in low demand there.
At the southern California border, prices were talked in the $1.91-1.94 range, while at Waha gas sold in the mid-$1.80s.
